article.name: Empirica
article.summary: Empirica is a local-first Python CLI and library for recording and evaluating an agent’s work beliefs, evidence, and outcomes. It uses SQLite for project records, Git notes for versioned history, and optional Qdrant for semantic retrieval. The three stores have different roles and can diverge; no runtime quality or performance was measured.

who_what.text: The official README describes Empirica as epistemic infrastructure for measuring agent beliefs, gating actions, and retaining learning across sessions. The repository is an open source Python CLI/library with harness integration; the README states an MIT license.

architecture.text: The architecture separates a queryable SQLite working record, commit-associated Git notes for durable history/transport, and optional Qdrant vectors for semantic retrieval. The project notes that these stores are written at different times and can disagree.

Typed artifacts include findings, unknowns, assumptions, decisions, mistakes, dead ends, goals, lessons, and sources. SQLite rows carry project and session relationships plus optional evidence/source references; separate Git note stores use per-type refs.

behavior.text: CLI artifact-log commands and repository methods create typed SQLite records with project/session and optional source/evidence links. Matching per-type Git note stores preserve commit-associated artifact history; Qdrant stores derived vectors when semantic features are enabled.

The lifecycle model resolves findings as stale, superseded, retracted, or mistyped; unknowns can be answered, assumptions verified/falsified/expired, goals completed, and decisions assessed. Supersession points to a named artifact, and ID helpers reject ambiguous prefixes. These are retained lifecycle states rather than an in-place factual edit API.

The canonical-storage guide describes note archival on delete and resolution stamping on active notes. Archival moves the Git note into an archive ref and removes it from the active ref after a successful archive write, preserving the archived note. The review found no cross-store erasure guarantee; bulk dead-end and mistake invalidations are documented as SQLite-only and can reappear after a from-notes rebuild.

Default Qdrant focused search covers docs, memory, eidetic facts, and episodic entries; intelligence search adds assumptions, decisions, and goals. Search is project-keyed and excludes resolved memory by default. Qdrant-unavailable searches return empty results; architecture documentation describes a keyword-search degradation path. Bootstrap also loads active project goals from SQLite.

SQLite reads and Qdrant collections are keyed by project_id, giving the inspected code paths project partitioning. The review did not find evidence that these IDs alone enforce authorization; filesystem, database, and remote Qdrant access control were not evaluated.

Artifact evidence references, source identifiers, lifecycle outcome events, and commit-associated notes provide traceability. Outcome bookkeeping is fail-open, and the inspected model does not make a source reference mandatory or prove claim truth.

Optional Qdrant collections are created lazily and can be absent without disabling SQLite-backed core functions. Architecture describes lower-capability keyword retrieval when semantic search is unavailable. README and architecture describe grading self-reported beliefs against external signals such as tests and commit activity; no performance or quality measurement was collected in this review.

limits.text: This review inspected official documentation and source at the verified main head. Empirica, its tests, and benchmarks were not run.
Retrieval quality, effective deployment authorization, cross-store consistency under failure, physical erasure across copies/backups, latency, and cost remain unknown from this source review.

benchmark.note: No Empirica runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Project metrics and the planned fixture are not Empirica results.
